text:
Marathon Petroleum rose modestly today, capping a remarkable two-week rally of over 11% that accelerated sharply in the past four trading days. The gains reflect a confluence of tailwinds for refiners: US crude oil prices at $96 a barrel, refineries humming at 92.5% capacity utilization, and forecasts from major banks predicting diesel prices will remain stubbornly high through 2027 due to tight refining capacity. High diesel margins are the lifeblood of refiner profits, and Goldman Sachs's view that this stays locked in for over a year gives the market reason to keep bidding up the stock.

The broader backdrop amplifies these fundamentals—geopolitical tensions in the Middle East (Iranian tanker attacks, Yemen operations) have kept global oil prices elevated at $114 a barrel, while low storage levels for both gasoline and diesel signal tight market conditions that favor refiners' margins. This is not a one-day story but a multi-month positioning shift as the market prices in sustained refining profitability.
